metadata.status: Provisional, structurally informed elicitation scenario; not validated high-confidence district estimates.
metadata.interpretation: All numerical centres and concentrations are analyst-selected assumptions, not estimates reported by the cited sources. Structural information supports qualitative comparisons but does not identify monthly rates or their precision. These priors should not be represented as an expert-validated calibration.

units.p: Monthly probability of exit under the supplied model definition.
units.gamma: Mean monthly arrivals divided by the under-5 population; fraction, not percent.
units.omega: Total standard deviation of monthly arrivals divided by the under-5 population; fraction, not percent.

construction.mean: For each Beta distribution, the centre is a/(a+b).
construction.p: Centres range from 0.18 to 0.35, using recovery-access assumptions. Concentration a+b is 100 for better-contextualized entries and 50 otherwise. No numerical case-fatality adjustment was made.
construction.gamma: The reference centre 0.006 and district centres 0.0035-0.009 are uncalibrated elicitation anchors chosen without outcome data. Relative contextual vulnerability shifts the centre; no numerical conversion from food insecurity, displacement, or livelihood indicators is claimed.
construction.omega: Centres 0.0018-0.0055 describe assumed real monthly variation. Information gaps broaden the prior rather than increase its centre.
construction.precision: For better-contextualized entries, gamma prior coefficient of variation is 0.20 and omega prior coefficient of variation is 0.25; otherwise these are 0.30 and 0.40. These precision choices implement an informative scenario and are not source-derived confidence.
construction.beta_conversion: Given a mean m and prior coefficient of variation c, k=(1-m)/(m*c*c)-1, a=m*k, b=(1-m)*k. Shape parameters are rounded to eight decimal places.
construction.dependence: The file supplies marginal priors only. Independence is an additional model assumption, not established by this elicitation.
construction.time_invariance: Centres describe assumed persistent conditions; no year-specific priors or peak-crisis calibration were used.

evidence_gaps.district_cmam_coverage: Not established for any district across the full period. Regional health-facility availability and humanitarian presence are imperfect proxies and do not demonstrate CMAM coverage, effectiveness, or supply continuity.
evidence_gaps.chronic_ipc_afi_baseline: Not established from a complete 2017-2021 sequence for any district. No district is assigned an asserted typical IPC AFI phase.
evidence_gaps.clinical_course: Context alone cannot identify whether rapid death or prolonged persistence dominates total exits. Lower p in constrained settings assumes recovery barriers dominate; mortality could reverse this ordering.
evidence_gaps.district_access: Access judgments combine regional context with selected historical examples; they are not verified five-year district access classifications.
evidence_gaps.displacement: Persistent hosting is supported most clearly for Mogadishu, Baidoa and Kismayo. Humanitarian offices or movement-monitoring locations elsewhere are not treated as proof of a district-wide high IDP share.
evidence_gaps.aggregation: Districts contain multiple livelihoods and population groups. No under-5 population-weighted livelihood mixture was estimated; district-wide centres are judgmental.
evidence_gaps.research_completeness: Selected structural sections and contextual excerpts were read, not every document in the requested multi-year sequence. Full district evidence extraction and independent clinical elicitation remain incomplete.

outcome_separation.used: Livelihood geography, food and income pathways, seasonal mechanisms, regional facility availability, humanitarian access context, and displacement context.
outcome_separation.excluded: No outcome figures, outcome rankings, derived caseloads or IPC Acute Malnutrition classifications were used in selecting hyperparameters.
outcome_separation.retrieval_limitation: Search results and mixed-source extracts incidentally exposed prohibited outcome material. It was discarded from the assessment; therefore this research session cannot be described as strictly blinded to all such material.
outcome_separation.temporal_scope: Current country-page narratives and post-2021 events were not used to characterize 2017-2021.

source_access_notes: FSNAU resources/tools returned an internal fetch error; the baseline archive and direct 2016 livelihood PDF were used instead.
Several FSNAU archive download links failed; direct non-www PDF links recovered the principal livelihood document and selected baselines.
OCHA Somalia country page returned HTTP 403; the separately indexed OCHA access section on the UN Somalia site was used instead.
The 2016 SARA catalogue was accessible, but its report download failed; WHO's 2018 Health Cluster Strategy service-availability section was used instead.
UNHCR 2018 year-end and May 2020 flood pages failed on direct opening; their indexed contextual excerpts and the accessible November 2020 fact sheet were used.
The IOM July 2019 regional PDF failed on direct opening; the DTM baseline series and UNHCR contextual evidence were used instead.

FSNAU publications index was accessible, but a selected climate-update link failed. A complete multi-year post-seasonal series was not safely reviewed; livelihood seasonal calendars provided the structural alternative.
West Golis health-search results mixed contextual statements with prohibited outcomes; that mixed passage was excluded. Restricted nutrition survey reports were not deliberately opened.
model_checks_and_limits: All 74 requested district names are represented once; all Beta shape parameters are positive.

Prior concentration cannot be justified solely by knowing structural characteristics. Refit with weaker concentrations and alternative numerical centres before relying on sparse-district posterior results.
Under bounded monthly arrival fractions, omega must satisfy omega^2 <= gamma*(1-gamma). Independent Beta marginals do not enforce this joint constraint; all chosen mean pairs satisfy it.

The supplied variance assumes monthly arrival innovations have no cross-month covariance. Persistent drought or displacement can violate that assumption even when their marginal variation is represented by omega.
Loss to follow-up is not necessarily a biological exit from the disease state. Its treatment as an exit requires an observation-process definition consistent with the prevalence counts.
Prior-predictive checks using actual district populations and the supplied likelihood remain necessary; these were unavailable and were not replaced by prevalence-based calibration.

districts.reasoning: Cowpea and Coastal Deeh livelihoods motivate an elevated gamma assumption. Regional access constraints motivate lower p, while rainfall sensitivity and possible trade interruptions motivate higher omega; district programme coverage remains unverified.

Riverine farming and proximity to Mogadishu provide competing food-access advantages and flood exposure. I assume intermediate p and elevated gamma, with seasonal river conditions and corridor disruptions increasing omega.

Juba livestock livelihoods motivate above-anchor gamma, while dispersed settlement and regional service constraints motivate modest p. Seasonal pasture changes and border-corridor disruption are the assumed drivers of omega.

Riverine and pastoral components motivate elevated gamma despite agricultural production opportunities. Regional service limitations constrain assumed p, while river fluctuations and recurrent displacement motivate higher omega.

Coastal and Juba rural livelihoods offer some diversification, but regional access constraints motivate elevated gamma and lower p. Seasonal production and uncertain transport continuity motivate higher omega.
West Golis livelihoods suggest a pastoral rather than purely urban food economy. I assume moderate p and below-anchor gamma, with rainfall and livestock-income seasonality sustaining nonzero omega.

Riverine, cowpea and coastal livelihood components provide multiple food sources but expose households to agricultural disruption. Corridor insecurity motivates intermediate p and elevated gamma; seasonal river and market conditions motivate omega.

Mogadishu's service concentration and persistent displacement hosting motivate relatively higher p alongside elevated gamma. Repeated arrivals, eviction-related disruption and unstable household earnings motivate appreciable omega despite urban markets.

Coastal Deeh and inland pastoral components motivate anchor-level gamma, with fishing offering only partial diversification. I assume modest p for dispersed communities and appreciable omega from rainfall and fishing seasonality.

Coastal trade and surrounding agricultural livelihoods motivate moderately elevated gamma under southern access constraints. Assumed p remains modest, while crop seasonality and disrupted transport motivate omega.

Baidoa's persistent displacement hosting motivates elevated gamma, while its humanitarian-hub role supports a relatively higher p assumption. Recurrent arrivals and rainfed livelihood shocks motivate higher omega.
